response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-18
CLINICAL INDICATION: Surveillance. History of treated colon adenocarcinoma. Assess for new pulmonary nodules.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. A. Rahimi (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-05-14. The prior report states lungs clear with no focal opacity. The prior images show the left and right hilar opacities described below, and the prior report does not mention them.
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Same view and projection, no rotation, adequate inspiration and exposure on both. Differences: image processing and display contrast differ slightly and the current image has a wider border, which limits judging subtle density change in the small hilar opacities. A belt and buckle overlie the upper abdomen on the prior only, so the upper abdomen below the diaphragm cannot be compared between studies.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None time-sensitive. Order of review: F1 (left hilar opacity), F4 (right hilar focus), F2 (right hilar focus).

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central. Carina and main bronchi unremarkable. Lungs well inflated with no consolidation, collapse or interstitial pattern. Vascular markings reach the chest wall bilaterally. Small, dense, well-defined rounded opacity at the lateral margin of the left hilum (F1), present on both films in the same position with similar shape, density and apparent size. Calcification cannot be confirmed on this study. No new lung opacity in any zone compared with the prior.
- Mediastinum / hila: Upper mediastinum not widened. Aortic knuckle and aortopulmonary window preserved. Hila normal in size and position, with no interval hilar enlargement. Small dense focus over the right hilum, present on both films with similar size and density. This is indeterminate: the two blind reads disagreed, with each read recording it as a separate finding (F2 from read A only, F4 from read B only). The indication pass describes F2 and F4 as the same focus. It may be a vessel seen end-on or a small calcified node.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles sharp. No pleural thickening. No effusion or pneumothorax on either study.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal to mildly prominent, with a rounded left ventricular contour. Heart borders sharp. Size and shape look the same as on the prior. Cardiothoracic ratio not measured; radiologist to measure in PACS.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture and no destructive bone lesion in the ribs, clavicles, shoulders or visible spine. Bilateral breast shadows overlie the lower zones. No soft tissue gas. No free gas under the diaphragm. No lines, tubes, ports, pacemaker or surgical clips.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: None. No new pulmonary nodule seen on the current film compared with the prior.
- Unchanged: Left hilar dense rounded opacity (F1), similar. Right hilar dense focus (F2/F4), similar, indeterminate because the reads disagreed. Cardiac silhouette, similar. Mediastinal contour and pleura, unchanged. No measurements are available, so size change is described in words only. Upper abdomen not comparable because of the belt and buckle on the prior.

RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the small dense left hilar opacity a calcified granuloma or node, or a non-calcified nodule? | Reason: The opacity is small, and a frontal film at this resolution cannot confirm calcification or show its margins in detail. It could also be a vessel end-on. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS and any older films. CT chest if calcification or long-term stability cannot be confirmed.
- Is the left perihilar nodule calcified, which would be consistent with a granuloma? | Reason: The nodule is small and these are downsampled frontal radiographs. Density and internal calcification cannot be confirmed at this resolution. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS and compare with any older studies to establish long-term stability. CT chest if calcification or stability cannot be confirmed.
- Is the small dense right hilar focus a calcified node or a vessel end-on? | Reason: On a single frontal projection, a small hilar density cannot be separated from a normal vessel seen end-on. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest if clinically relevant.
- Is the small dense focus over the right hilum a vessel end-on, a calcified node or a small nodule? | Reason: It is a small density superimposed on hilar vessels on a frontal view alone, and the image resolution is limited. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with a lateral view if available. CT chest if it remains unexplained.
- Is there a retrocardiac or retrosternal abnormality? | Reason: Only frontal films were provided. The area behind the heart is seen through the cardiac shadow only. | Recommend: Lateral view if there is clinical concern.
- Is there a retrocardiac or hidden lower lobe abnormality? | Reason: Only frontal views are provided, and the retrocardiac region is partly obscured by the prominent cardiac silhouette. | Recommend: Lateral view.
- Does the prominent left heart border reflect enlargement of a specific chamber or of the pulmonary artery? | Reason: A frontal radiograph shows the contour only. It cannot separate the left atrial appendage, the pulmonary artery segment and normal variation. | Recommend: Lateral chest view and clinical correlation. Echocardiography if clinically indicated.

IMPRESSION:
1. Small dense well-defined rounded left hilar opacity (F1), similar to the prior. Calcification not confirmed, so granuloma or node versus non-calcified nodule is undetermined.
2. Small dense focus over the right hilum (F4, F2), similar to the prior. Indeterminate, as the two reads disagreed. Calcified node versus vessel end-on is undetermined.
3. No new pulmonary nodule seen compared with the prior on frontal views. Small or retrocardiac nodules cannot be excluded on frontal views alone.
4. Cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal to mildly prominent, similar to the prior. Chamber or pulmonary artery enlargement cannot be determined on a frontal view.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review source images in PACS and any older films for the left and right hilar opacities. Measure the cardiothoracic ratio in PACS.
- CT chest if calcification or long-term stability of the hilar opacities cannot be confirmed. No interval is specified in the findings; the attending to set it.
- Lateral chest view if there is clinical concern for a retrocardiac, retrosternal or lower lobe abnormality or for the cardiac contour. No interval is specified in the findings.
- Echocardiography if clinically indicated.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
